feedback:
This revision closes most of what the last round left open, and I verified each of those against the current text rather than taking the claim on trust. Diarization and note generation are now run stages with kinds, cancellation entries and recovery transitions (D-006, D-007, D-031), so D-031's universal-coverage claim is no longer false. Diarization has its own sandboxed service and enters residency accounting (D-003, D-027). The delivery predicate is content-based, so the equal-length replacement that previously produced a false rejection is handled, and D-010 now has a terminal delivered state with a launch sweep that only touches genuinely uncertain rows. D-030 fsyncs encoded bytes before the index record that names them, carries per-packet sizes and a CRC, and rejects a torn tail by prefix validation. D-038 supplies the archived state that makes runtime replacement bound storage while History stays attributable, which the previous garbage-collection rule could not do. D-014 makes list order the whole precedence rule. D-036 converts the distribution question into a decision on the basis the specification itself supplies, so no blocking question stands against an architecture that already assumed the answer. D-025 confines automatic resumption to adapters that identify the player and observe the transition, which satisfies the ownership clause. D-011 no longer degrades to waveform-only, D-033 names session-directory ownership before the History row exists, and D-012's split check set stops pack coverage from restricting which models a user may run. Those objections no longer apply.

What remains is smaller than the last round but still blocks acceptance. Verified against the current text:

Delivery can still insert twice. D-009 lets an unchanged readback after Command-V count as an explicit negative and unlock rung 3. Readability is not acknowledgment: RESEARCH states that posting a paste event supplies no general acknowledgment that the target consumed the clipboard, and REVIEW_NOTES records precisely this delayed-consumer case. A consumer that applies the paste after the readback, followed by synthesized typing, duplicates the paragraph. Separately, the target is resolved once in D-008, while Command-V, typing and the submit Return are posted events that reach whatever is focused when each is posted, so a focus change between rungs or before Return is undefined. Rung-specific fallthrough rules and revalidation immediately before each posted event would resolve both.

Meeting-note provenance is not representable. result_inputs holds an input_result_id with roles in {transcript, diarization, prior_notes}, and a speaker_assignment_revision is not a result and has no role, yet D-037 says it is recorded there and verification asserts an invariant requiring it. The initial meeting run compounds this: one meeting run runs from arming through noting, its manifest is written and fsynced at arming, and the diarization result and assignment revision do not exist then, so the values D-037 says the notes run pins cannot be in that manifest. Recovery from noting reads the manifest to know which inputs stand. Either a separate notes run created after its inputs commit, or a committed manifest extension, plus a dependency representation that can name a non-result entity.

The question protection has no mechanism when a pack is missing. Interrogative detection sits in the language-dependent set, and the no-pack disposition then turns on whether the transcript contains an interrogative marker. Marker detection is not in the enumerated language-independent set, so the safety path depends on a check the design has just declared unavailable. This is repairable by putting a punctuation-level marker check in the independent set with its limits stated.

The preview ladder does not answer the case it is cited for. D-027 permits one resident speech model, D-004 sends a denied provisional pass to D-011, and both of D-011's fallback rungs require speech inference. When batch work holds the speech slot, no rung runs, yet D-011 and the Recording display coverage entry both claim the ladder still produces text under admission denial. Reserved preview capacity or batch speech preemption would close it. Nearby: imports enter the capturing stage while D-004 calls them batch work and exempts the capture writer and sealer from admission, so an import's ingest path has no stated lane, and nothing bounds the number of concurrent runs, each of which holds windows, a journal and buffers outside the model budget.

Opt-in context retention has no home. The schema lists context_digests and nothing else, while D-016 promises retained text shown in History and deleted with the recording. The specification's instruction not to defer persistent-data decisions applies directly here.

D-030's recovery sequence is written in the wrong order: it builds the pakt chunk from accepted records and then appends re-encoded surviving chunks, which leaves the table stale. F3's injection points also stop at the two per-chunk fsyncs and do not cover the finalization writes (pakt, data-size patch, hash, final fsync), which is where the remaining ambiguity sits.

The unattributed play-pause path is a toggle. D-025's rationale says pausing something unknown costs nothing if nothing was playing, but the recorded failure is different and is in REVIEW_NOTES: a paused player can receive the toggle while an unrelated client keeps the output device active, which starts playback. A one-way pause command to an identified player, or no automatic action for unsupported players, would resolve it.

F1's retention criterion is circular. The default is retained if it is within 15 percent of the fallback adapter, and the action on failure is to build that adapter, which D-020 says is built when F1 rules the first choice out. The comparison cannot decide anything until both exist, and equivalent model is undefined across Core ML and GGML. Two-stream alignment drift is measured with no acceptance range and no action, although D-001's reconsideration condition lets that measurement move the macOS baseline.

Three of the review's objections I judge overstated. D-028's fallback does what REVIEW_NOTES asked, which was that a failed access method must not silently relax the contract: the narrowed claim text is written in advance and the guarantee changes visibly. The residual is wording, since calling a symbol scan verification contradicts RESEARCH's statement that such a scan cannot establish absence of network access; the sentence should describe it as corroborating rather than verifying. The demand that diarization quality become a ship gate runs against the specification's rule that model evaluation must not become a feature gate, and the design already states what a monotonicity result would change. The demand that every numeric range carry a derivation goes past what the specification asks; assigning approval authority and a failure action is a defensible basis, and the real defect inside that objection is the F1 circularity above. On raw prose context, absolute enforcement is unsatisfiable by any design and the proposal bounds its claim honestly, but the asymmetry does need an answer: screen and clipboard text are distilled because they may carry instructions, while focused-element text is always prose, and no reason is given why that source is safer.

Smaller items worth folding in: D-022 does not say whether tokenizers and other companion assets participate in the identity hash, and no run pins the runtime or adapter revision, so two results can share an installation identity and different behavior. D-038 retains per-asset notices while releasing blobs, but D-022 stores the notice path without saying it lives outside Models/blobs, so archiving may delete what it claims to keep. D-033 reclaims stale leases without defining staleness. D-015 combines ordered rules with longest match first without saying which dominates.

Not stuck. Every confirmed defect is fixable inside this design with material already available, and none requires an experiment or a product decision the inputs cannot support.
